source.title: When and Why Momentum Accelerates SGD: An Empirical Study
source.authors: Jingwen Fu; Bo-Han Wang; Hui-Shuai Zhang; Zhi-Zheng Zhang; Wei Chen; Na Zheng

record.file_problem: none; full paper text, including appendices, is present
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own training-loss comparisons and training dynamics for SGD and momentum under varied learning rates and batch sizes. These bear on the training-behavior claim, but use optimizer comparisons and loss measures rather than the claim versions’ specified training-error outcomes.
record.gate_note: Results are about loss, training speed, oscillation, and directional Hessian, not training classification error or zero error. Figures 2–13 are the reported experimental results; precise plotted values are not transcribed. The 60-row limit does not bind.
record.test_reason: The study directly bears on V5's full-batch edge-of-stability component: it measures training loss and Hessian sharpness using the fc-tanh network and CIFAR-10-5k setup used by Cohen et al. Its optimizer comparisons do not test the other versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors find that momentum's acceleration emerges beyond effective-learning-rate and batch-size thresholds and attribute it to preventing or delaying abrupt directional sharpening and EoS entry. They acknowledge limited architecture and dataset coverage; Adam receives only preliminary appendix experiments.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares SGD and momentum variants using matched effective learning rates, fixed hyperparameters, and training-loss trajectories; it does not test the original claim’s training-classification-error criterion. The paper is an empirical optimizer study.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported training-loss relationship changes with effective learning rate, batch size, momentum coefficient, architecture, dataset, and epoch budget. The authors state deviation points differ among datasets and momentum’s effect varies across architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: At matched effective learning rates, momentum's training-loss advantage emerges beyond learning-rate or batch-size thresholds and varies across architectures and datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Momentum accelerates training chiefly at larger effective learning rates and batch sizes under the tested constant-hyperparameter recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: Momentum and smaller batches prevent or delay abrupt directional sharpening; tested Nesterov momentum enters EoS earlier than Polyak momentum.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Momentum and stochastic gradients can delay abrupt directional sharpening, with the delay depending on optimizer choice.

record.problems: The authors say architecture and dataset coverage is not comprehensive; experiments primarily use constant learning rates and momentum and use training loss as a proxy for training speed. Most reported results are qualitative descriptions of figures without exact values, error bars, or uncertainty estimates. Adam is only preliminary and excluded from the paper's main focus.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error, corrupted or random labels, and model-size or regularization qualifications.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
Depth degradation, identity shortcuts, deep plain tanh training, and Fixup.
Activation-matched initialization, signal propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and trainable depth.

Recovery above the initial linearized-model stability limit with squared loss, the catapult curvature drop, divergence at larger rates, and divergence despite starting below threshold. Exact sharpness plateau values and long-horizon behavior cannot be assessed from the supplied figure descriptions.
Matched comparisons of training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, and Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The record incorrectly excludes V5 entirely. Directional Hessian alone would be insufficient, but the study also reports maximum-eigenvalue sharpness and full-batch loss trajectories. Momentum's delayed EoS entry is an additional optimizer result, not evidence against ordinary GD's reported EoS behavior. No numerical plot values were inferred.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, random or corrupted labels, CIFAR-10/100 error outcomes, model size, and early stopping are not measured.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student setup, spurious minima, or width comparison.
No plain versus residual shortcut depth comparison or training-error comparison.
No initialization comparison or initialization-dependent training speed/depth test.

No learning-rate-above-stability-limit recovery claim is tested. Learning rates are compared via effective learning rate; the paper studies oscillation and abrupt sharpening, not the stated curvature-drop recovery or full-batch sharpness hovering claim.

rows.subject: VGG13-BN
rows.operation_detail: Compared SGD and SGDM training losses across effective learning rates at batch size 1024 for 200 epochs; SGDM momentum coefficients were 0, 0.5, and 0.9.

conditions.value: training loss after T epochs by effective learning rate

rows.measure: Training loss after 200 epochs, compared across effective learning rates
rows.baseline: SGD (µ=0) at the same effective learning rate
rows.value: For small effective learning rates, different µ settings perform almost the same; beyond thresholds, curves with small µ deviate from large µ, and SGDM performs better than or equivalent to SGD.
rows.note: The paper describes qualitative curve behavior; exact plotted values are not stated. This measures training loss/speed, not classification error.
rows.check: Momentum comparisons of endpoint training loss do not establish any version's effect; partial is not an applicable claim state.

rows.subject: VGG13-BN
rows.operation_detail: Compared SGD and SGDM across momentum coefficients and batch sizes at matched effective learning rates for 200 epochs.
rows.measure: Training loss by effective learning rate and batch size
rows.baseline: SGD with µ=0 at the matched effective learning rate and batch size
rows.value: Reducing batch size has a similar pattern to adding momentum; SGDM-SGD gap grows with batch size; among SGDM settings, batch-size gaps shrink with larger momentum coefficient.
rows.note: The paper gives qualitative comparisons, not numeric plotted values. It reports several varying conditions in prose.
rows.check: Batch-size and momentum comparisons do not measure a listed version's effect.

rows.subject: VGG13-BN
rows.operation_detail: Varied batch size while fixing effective learning rate and compared training losses across momentum coefficients.

conditions.value: gradually increased; exact values not stated

rows.value: At small batch sizes, different µ settings perform almost the same; beyond a threshold batch size, larger µ tends to perform better. Momentum extends the range where the linear scaling law holds.
rows.note: Qualitative description; precise values and the threshold are not stated.
rows.check: The linear scaling range is not a listed claim. The effective learning rate is specifically referenced to batch size 1024.

rows.subject: fc-tanh
rows.operation_detail: Compared full-batch GD and GDM training loss across effective learning rates and tracked loss trajectories at selected rates.
rows.measure: Training loss and oscillation over epochs
rows.value: At effective learning rate 0.01, curves are smooth and closely aligned; at 0.1, they align initially, then GD oscillates and deviates, with GD slower than GDM at the same time oscillation starts.
rows.note: The text reports the qualitative trajectories; exact loss values are not stated.
rows.check: Link the full-batch GD trajectory at effective learning rate 0.1 to V5's edge-of-stability component, together with R5. Oscillation accompanies slower continuing loss reduction. The 0.01 trajectory and GDM comparison are controls, not absent effects.

rows.subject: fc-tanh
rows.operation_detail: Measured directional Hessian along update direction and sharpness during GD/GDM training.

conditions.value: small rate, exact value not stated

rows.measure: Directional Hessian and sharpness over training
rows.value: At small effective learning rate, directional Hessians of GD and GDM are around 0. At larger rate, GD has abrupt sharpening and oscillates while GDM directional Hessian stays around 0; at an even larger rate, both exhibit abrupt sharpening, later for GDM.
rows.note: The paper describes qualitative plot behavior; precise plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: The row omits the key maximum-Hessian-eigenvalue result: Figure 6 reports GD sharpness crossing 2/ηef when oscillation and abrupt directional sharpening begin. Separate maximum-eigenvalue sharpness from directional Hessian, and split the small, larger, and largest learning-rate conditions. The current condition incorrectly describes only the small-rate case.

rows.subject: fc-tanh
rows.operation_detail: Compared GD, GDM, and SGD at batch size 250 and measured loss and abrupt sharpening.
rows.measure: Training curves and entry into edge-of-stability / abrupt sharpening
rows.baseline: GD and GDM compared with SGD
rows.value: GD enters EoS during training, while SGD and GDM do not and remain well-aligned throughout training; the paper states stochastic noise can defer abrupt sharpening.
rows.note: Qualitative descriptions only; exact values are not stated.
rows.check: The full-batch GD condition explicitly enters edge of stability. Separate that result from the SGD and GDM comparisons; their avoidance of entry during the observed interval does not challenge V5. The effective learning rate uses reference batch size 5000.

rows.subject: SGDM with Nesterov's momentum
rows.operation_detail: Compared training behavior over effective learning rates under settings matching Figure 3; also compared with Polyak momentum at effective learning rate 1.0.

conditions.value: settings same as Figure 3; exact values not stated
same µ for Polyak comparison; exact value not stated

rows.measure: Training loss pattern and timing of EoS entry
rows.baseline: Polyak momentum at same µ for the direct comparison
rows.value: Nesterov behaves similarly in the align-and-deviate comparison and can prevent abrupt sharpening; under the 1.0 comparison it enters EoS earlier and performs worse than Polyak.
rows.note: The paper cautions that more extensive experiments are needed before a conclusive claim about Nesterov momentum.
rows.check: This bundles two experiments: Figure 8 uses VGG13-BN on CIFAR-10 under Figure 3's setup; Figure 9 uses full-batch fc-tanh on CIFAR-10-5k under Figure 5's setup. Relative EoS entry times for momentum variants do not alone establish V5's sharpness-and-loss trajectory.

rows.value: The align-and-deviate pattern also exists in Adam as effective learning rate increases.
rows.note: The text reports a qualitative pattern; exact curve values are not stated.
rows.check: Adam's align-and-deviate loss pattern does not establish threshold crossing, curvature dynamics, or recovery in V5. Identify the model as fc-tanh and Adam as its optimizer.

relationships.condition: Full-batch GD on fc-tanh with CIFAR-10-5k at the larger tested effective learning rate.
relationships.reason: R4–R6 report continuing, oscillatory loss reduction and entry into EoS as maximum-eigenvalue sharpness crosses 2/ηef; this qualitatively supports V5's full-batch component.
relationships.display_finding: Loss continued decreasing with oscillations as maximum-eigenvalue sharpness crossed 2/ηef and training entered the edge of stability.
